technical_and_design_decisions: User stories U3 and U4 are textual duplicates describing the same feature; the work is consolidated into a single activity to avoid double counting.

The increment targets the Spring XD project (a Spring ecosystem data integration framework), not Spring Framework core. New modules follow the existing 'stream' module pattern (source/processor/sink) using the Spring XD Module SPI and Java-based module options.
U1 and U7 share a similar processor-module design pattern; both follow the existing Spark/Analytics processor conventions, with options-driven configuration and Tuple-based data handling.

U2 is treated as a non-functional dependency upgrade whose primary cost is in fixing compile-time and test breakage caused by Reactor 2.0 RC1 API changes (e.g., Observable/Mono naming and operator changes).
U5 is implemented by creating a sibling Maven module for Hadoop-dependent tests and removing the hadoop-* dependencies from the DIRT module, leaving only a test-scope dependency declaration.

U6 uses an existing CI infrastructure pattern (e.g., EC2-hosted Jenkins slaves running cloud-init scripts to provision XD + YARN clusters) and ports pre-existing acceptance tests rather than authoring them from scratch.

U8 is implemented by exposing the maxContentLength value on the HttpChunkAggregator via a module option that reads from servers.yml, with a sensible default (1MB) preserved for backward compatibility.
The developer is assumed to be senior, already familiar with the Spring XD codebase, Reactor 1.x, RxJava, Spring Data Redis, and YARN. No ramp-up or onboarding time is included.
Documentation updates are scoped to the Reference Guide (Asciidoc) and inline Javadoc; no marketing or release-notes work is included.
assumptions: U3 and U4 are duplicate user stories describing the same deliverable; they are estimated once.
Redis is available as a managed service in the dev/test environment; no Redis server provisioning is required.
EC2 infrastructure for U6 already exists in the CI environment; the work covers authoring and wiring the acceptance tests, not standing up new infrastructure.
Reactor 2.0 RC1 has documented release notes available; no time is spent reverse-engineering the API.
Unit tests use existing test harnesses; integration tests run against embedded Redis/HDFS where feasible.
All estimates represent coding hours by a single experienced developer; meetings, code reviews, and waiting time are excluded.
The Hadoop test isolation (U5) is a low-risk refactor with no functional change to behavior; effort is bounded to module/POM restructuring and Eclipse CP verification.
Hadoop dependency artifacts (hadoop-client, hadoop-yarn-api, etc.) are already declared in the parent POM and can be reused in the new test module without adding new artifacts.

activities.activity_name: U1 — Reactor-based processor module (design, implementation, tests)
activities.activity_description: Research the existing Spark and Analytics processor module patterns, design a Reactor-based ProcessorModule with module options (e.g., processor class, parallelism), implement the module and its options metadata, write unit tests, and add a stream integration test in the XD test harness.

Review Reactor 2.0 RC1 release notes and breaking changes, update the Reactor dependency in the parent and module POMs, fix compile-time breakage across affected modules, and update/correct unit tests impacted by the new API surface.

activities.activity_name: U3/U4 — Redis field-value counter aggregation: spec port & gap analysis
activities.activity_description: Read the linked OLD Aggregate Field-Value Counters wiki spec, port the relevant design into the new codebase, identify gaps relative to current Redis abstractions, and write a short design note covering field selection, counter keying, and aggregation cadence.

activities.activity_name: U3/U4 — Redis field-value counter aggregation: implementation
activities.activity_description: Implement the aggregate processor module and the field-value-counter sink module using Spring Data Redis, including continuous write semantics, configurable TTL/cadence, and proper handling of counter types (long/double).

activities.activity_name: U3/U4 — Redis field-value counter aggregation: tests
activities.activity_description: Write unit tests for aggregation correctness and an integration test using embedded Redis (or a test container) that verifies continuous write behavior as new data is ingested.

activities.activity_name: U3/U4 — Redis field-value counter aggregation: reference documentation
activities.activity_description: Update the Spring XD Reference Guide with a new section covering the aggregate processor and field-value-counter sink, including module options, example stream definitions, and operational notes (key expiry, cardinality).

activities.activity_name: U5 — Isolate Hadoop tests in a separate project
activities.activity_description: Create a new Maven module for Hadoop-dependent tests, move Hadoop-specific integration tests into it, prune the hadoop-* dependencies from the DIRT module's runtime scope, verify the Eclipse classpath no longer pulls in Hadoop artifacts incorrectly, and ensure mvn verify passes from a clean checkout.

activities.activity_name: U6 — XD + YARN acceptance tests on EC2: design & wiring
activities.activity_description: Review the existing acceptance test framework, design the EC2 provisioning flow (cloud-init or user-data bootstrap) to bring up an XD-on-YARN cluster, define the test matrix (container start, source/processor/sink round-trip, shutdown), and wire the suite into the CI job definition.

activities.activity_name: U6 — XD + YARN acceptance tests on EC2: implementation
activities.activity_description: Author the acceptance test scenarios targeting simple XD features (time/source, transform/processor, hdfs/sink) running on a YARN-provisioned container, with EC2 lifecycle handling (spin up cluster, run tests, tear down).

activities.activity_name: U6 — XD + YARN acceptance tests on EC2: CI integration
activities.activity_description: Hook the new acceptance suite into the existing EC2-backed Jenkins job, add nightly/per-build triggers, and configure log/artifact collection for failure debugging.

activities.activity_name: U7 — RxJava-based processor module (design, implementation, tests)
activities.activity_description: Study the RxJava 1.x API, design a ProcessorModule that lets users wire Observable-based computations, expose module options (input/output class, processor class), implement the module and the bridging from the XD message channel to Observables, and add unit + integration tests.

activities.activity_name: U8 — HTTP source configurable max message size (impl + tests + docs)
activities.activity_description: Refactor the HTTP source module to read maxContentLength from a module option (default 1MB), add the option to servers.yml override support, update the related PR/branch, add a unit/integration test that exceeds the default to verify the override, and document the option in the Reference Guide.

activities.activity_name: Cross-cutting: full build, integration verification, and docs sweep
activities.activity_description: Run the full multi-module Maven build, execute the complete integration test suite (XD distribution, single-node, and the EC2 acceptance suite as available locally), triage and fix any cross-module regressions introduced by the Reactor upgrade and new modules, and perform a final pass on Reference Guide cross-references and Javadoc.
